newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: FORECAST - Czech June trade deficit seen lower.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Czech June trade deficit seen lower.

text.p: The Czech Republic's trade deficit will show further signs of improvement when June figures are released on Tuesday morning as the weaker crown boosts exports, a Reuters survey of economists said.

The average forecast in the poll, conducted on Monday, was for a June trade deficit of 10.5 billion crowns with estimates ranging from eight billion crowns at the most optimistic end to a maximum of 14 billion crowns.
Only one analyst in the survey, Zivnostneska Banka's Pavel Sobisek, expected June's figure to exceed the May trade deficit of 11 billion crowns.
"There will be two effects which will combine...one factor will be a weaker crown which will boost crown revenues from exports," said Sobisek whose estimate was 14 billion crowns.

"On the other hand, the May figure was influenced by the fact that import deposits started to take effect and it may have postponed some imports...Maybe some postponed imports from May could have been realised in June. That's why I believe that actually the deficit will slightly widen against May."

In mid-April the government responded to mounting concern about the trade deficit by imposing a requirement on exporters that they deposit a sum equal to 20 percent of the value of their imports in non-interest bearing accounts at Czech banks.

Subsequently, the crown came under speculative attack from abroad forcing the central bank to float it. Since then, it has fallen by six percent against the mark and 13 percent against the dollar to 19.2 and 34.4 to the crown respectively.

Despite a marked improvement in the trade deficit in recent months heavy flooding affecting around a third of the country has heightned fears that imports of industrial and agricultural goods may take off later in the year.
None of those participating in Monday's poll expected there to be any effect of the flooding on June's figures.
"I don't exclude that we will have to correct our (full year 1997) forecast later this year but I think it would be premature to do it now," said Martin Kupka of Patria Finance.

The Czech Statistical Office (CSU) recently revised downwards its full year 1997 trade deficit forecast to between 160 and 180 billion crowns from a previous estimate of 190-200 billion crowns. The 1996 deficit was 159.8 billion crowns.

Foreign currency dealers' estimates tended to converge around the 10.5 billion crown average for June. Petr Kukla of Girocredit Banka said the crown was unlikely to strengthen by much even if the figures were far better than expected.

"Immediately the crown would strengthen but everyone knows that the flooding was really bad and that it's going to affect the economy badly. So we are not going to see the crown below 19.0 (to the mark) any time soon even if the trade deficit was five billion," he said.
